content: This annex to the Consolidated Key Population Guidelines provides detailed case studies showcasing effective practices from national, community-based, and community-led programs worldwide. These programs focus on key population groups that often face structural and societal barriers to accessing health and social services. The case studies offer practical examples of how community and healthcare providers can deliver accessible and acceptable services to these populations. The case studies highlight work on critical enablers, which are essential for facilitating access to services and creating an enabling environment for key populations. These enablers include reviewing laws and policies (such as decriminalization and age of consent), reducing stigma and discrimination, preventing violence, and empowering communities. The case studies also illustrate innovative approaches to service delivery that enhance the uptake of HIV services, harm reduction services, and retention in care. Many of the program descriptions include practical details on implementation strategies, and contact information is provided for all listed programs. The selected case studies demonstrate that focusing on critical enablers and improving service delivery for key population groups can positively impact individual and public health outcomes. The compilation of case studies achieves five objectives: identifying successful prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care services tailored to the needs of key populations; identifying key aspects of good practice in program design, implementation, and monitoring; showcasing programs addressing the needs of young people and adolescents in key populations; highlighting gaps in reaching key population groups, including young and adolescent members; and complementing the Consolidated Key Population Guidelines with practical examples for strengthening critical enablers and service delivery. The methodology for selecting case studies involved an online survey shaped by a review of current literature. The survey solicited examples of programs providing services to key populations, including adults and young people. Prospective contributors were invited to participate via a web link distributed to a wide network of relevant stakeholders, including WHO regional offices, UN partners, key population networks, NGOs, and program implementers. Participation was voluntary, and organizations could choose to remain anonymous in publicly available documents. The survey was available in multiple languages and closed in December 2013. Incomplete surveys or those lacking program names or contact information were excluded. Remaining surveys were translated into English if necessary, and exclusion criteria were applied to ensure the data's suitability for inclusion as case studies. Programs with fewer than 10 clients per month, those not addressing key populations, or those lacking monitoring and evaluation were excluded. Potential case studies were screened for regional, national, and intervention type representation, as well as evidence of appropriate monitoring and evaluation. Approximately 100 programs were invited to submit written case studies following a defined format, and nearly 90 programs submitted drafts. Further follow-up and editing resulted in the inclusion of 38 case studies in the Consolidated Key Population Guidelines and Technical Briefs, with an additional 31 case studies included in this annex. The case studies represent a range of services and interventions, including HIV testing and counseling, STI screening and treatment, antiretroviral therapy (ART), needle and syringe programs (NSP), opioid substitution therapy (OST), advocacy, and social and economic support. Around 75% of submissions reported conducting monitoring and evaluation activities, though only about half provided internal or external evaluation reports. Submissions were screened for geographical and programmatic representation, and follow-up information was requested for further consideration. The programs serve diverse key populations, including men who have sex with men (MSM), sex workers (SW), people who inject drugs (PWID), transgender individuals (TG), and individuals in prisons or other closed settings. Some programs serve multiple groups, such as MSM and TG, or all five key population groups. The programs also address the needs of young key populations (YKP), targeting individuals aged 10–24 years. The case studies are organized into two sections: those addressing critical enablers and those illustrating different approaches to service delivery. Each case study provides a brief description of the program, including its purpose, focus area, and key activities. Most case studies also highlight successes and challenges, with some detailing how challenges were addressed or resolved. Programs emphasize the importance of accessible, youth-friendly community spaces and the meaningful participation of key populations in program design and implementation. Examples include the Mpowerment project, which targets young gay men through community engagement and educational programming on HIV, sexual health, and harm reduction within social events. Another example is the National AIDS Control Programme (NACP) in Afghanistan, which provides harm reduction services for people who inject drugs while addressing stigma, discrimination, and police violence. Similarly, the Bridging the Gap program in Nepal focuses on advocacy and empowerment for people who inject drugs, engaging stakeholders across all levels to address health and human rights issues. These case studies demonstrate the importance of innovative, community-driven approaches to improving health outcomes for key populations while addressing structural and societal barriers.
